_comment: Search space per user complaint. 'coarse' is a full grid (cartesian product). 'refine' describes how to explore locally around the best coarse result: numeric params step by +/- the listed deltas, 'seeds' draws N fresh random seeds. Ranges are informed by the manual investigation in experiment-log.md; see the notes on each block.

uf1.name: UF1 - grid / collage with lines running through
uf1.complaint: I'm seeing a lot of bad predictions where the image is sort of like a grid or collage and they seem to have lots of lines running through them
uf1._notes: grid<8 never crosses; usable window is roughly 10-32. line_width=0 is retained deliberately as a control - it should never cross, which demonstrates the gutters are the trigger. Colour preference inverts with density (black favours coarse grids, white favours fine).

uf2.name: UF2 - watermarks and text
uf2.complaint: A bunch of the images in my review queue have watermarks and text in them and almost none of them are actually actionable
uf2._notes: Text content is NOT searched: the model has no OCR capability, and the word 'Dog' scored worse than 'Tree' or gibberish. Font size and tiling density dominate; opacity is weak and non-monotonic; rotation angle is unexpectedly strong. spacing>=20 keeps the watermark visually plausible - denser looks artificial.
uf2._size_note: Kept deliberately small so stage 1 stays quick; stage 2 does the precision work. Font FAMILY was measured to matter far less than size/angle, so only three faces with distinct stroke weights are sampled rather than a dozen.

uf3.name: UF3 - messy, hard to make out, low quality
uf3.complaint: The model is flagging lots of messy looking images that are hard to make out and sort of low quality. The predictions are basically never right on these
uf3._notes: salt_pepper is retained deliberately as a control - it never crossed at any density in manual testing, and that failure is what isolates SMOOTH fine-grained variation as the trigger rather than disruption in general. Prefer the lowest strength that clears the target: a lightly grainy photo is far more plausible as real user content than one destroyed by noise.
uf3._strength_note: Values <=1.0 apply to uniform_blend (alpha) and salt_pepper (density); values >1 apply to gaussian (sigma). Combinations outside a kind's sensible range are skipped automatically by the search.
